markingScheme.criterion: States that the deciding feature is cell type: bacteria cells are prokaryotic (no nucleus; genetic material free in the cytoplasm), while all four other kingdoms are eukaryotic (a nucleus enclosed in a membrane).
markingScheme.accept: 'No nucleus' for prokaryotic and 'has a nucleus' for eukaryotic are acceptable without the technical terms.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains why nutrition mode cannot be the deciding feature, because it varies within kingdoms too (e.g. some bacteria photosynthesise like plants; fungi and protoctista also feed in different ways), yet organisms are still grouped by cell type first.
markingScheme.insufficient: Restating 'bacteria feed differently' without explaining why nutrition varies within kingdoms and so cannot be the deciding feature.

markingScheme.criterion: Refers to their own Investigation Record evidence: the bacteria specimen showed no visible nucleus under the microscope while the amoeba (a eukaryote) clearly showed one, and states this is the same prokaryote/eukaryote split separating Bacteria from every other kingdom.
markingScheme.accept: Any correct reference to their own two microscope specimen results, even if not word-for-word.
markingScheme.insufficient: Mentioning the microscope specimens without stating what was or wasn't seen (the nucleus).

markingScheme.criterion: Correctly identifies the kingdom as Bacteria, because the organism has no nucleus (it is prokaryotic).
markingScheme.insufficient: Naming any other kingdom, or naming Bacteria with no reason given.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains that being able to photosynthesise does not override this: real bacteria (cyanobacteria) photosynthesise in exactly this way and are still classified as Bacteria because they lack a nucleus.
markingScheme.accept: Any correct example (real or reasoned) showing that nutrition mode does not override cell type.

markingScheme.criterion: States explicitly that cell type (not nutrition mode) is the general deciding evidence for classification, ideally naming this as the same reasoning microbiologists use for newly discovered microorganisms.
markingScheme.insufficient: Repeating 'no nucleus = Bacteria' without stating the general rule that cell type outweighs nutrition mode.

levels.descriptor: No specimens or evidence from the Investigation Record referenced.
Mentions a specimen or feature but does not connect it to the claim being made.

Clearly cites specific specimens and diagnostic features from the Investigation Record and uses them precisely to justify the classification.

criteria.source: = the Apply question's 3-point marking scheme above, one-to-one (correct kingdom named, photosynthesis-overridden argument, general cell-type rule stated). Do not award these 3 marks a second time here.

levels.descriptor: No attempt to reason about why cell type outweighs nutrition mode.
States a conclusion (e.g. 'it is Bacteria') but does not explain why.
Explains why, with one gap in the scientific logic (e.g. not addressing why nutrition mode is misleading).
Explains fully and correctly why cell type (prokaryotic vs eukaryotic), not nutrition mode, is the deciding evidence.

criteria.source: Assessed holistically across BOTH the Explain and Apply answers together — independent of, and never overlapping with, the content marks in use_of_evidence and reasoning above.

levels.descriptor: Unclear or missing sentences; no scientific terms.
Understandable but with unclear phrasing or missing key terms.
Clear, well-formed sentences using correct scientific vocabulary (e.g. 'prokaryotic', 'eukaryotic', 'heterotrophic').

markingInstructions: Mark ONLY the two constructed responses (Explain, Apply). Award marks point-by-point using each question's markingScheme in marking_context: each point is worth the marks stated, is independent unless it names a dependsOn point (in which case only award it if that earlier point was also awarded), and each point's 'accept'/'insufficient' tell you exactly what does and doesn't count. use_of_evidence's 3 marks ARE the Explain markingScheme's 3 points, and reasoning's 3 marks ARE the Apply markingScheme's 3 points — the rubric levels restate the same points as bands; award each set of 3 marks ONCE, not twice. communication is a separate, holistic 2 marks across both answers' clarity and vocabulary, never overlapping with the content marks. The Knowledge Check is already auto-marked in auto_marked_score — copy it into knowledge_accuracy (6 marks = full). Accept scientifically valid alternative wording (e.g. 'has no nucleus' for 'prokaryotic', 'makes its own food' for 'autotrophic'). Do not penalise spelling unless meaning is unclear. Total is out of 11 (6 auto + 3 + 3 + 2); report the percentage, one strength, one correction, and one next step, in under 80 words.
